# Wiki Section Disposition

A template's `Disposition:` line decides which of its sections an authored page may drop, so a page type's output structure is deterministic. This lookup holds the forms that line takes and the rules every section of a page meets.

**See also:** `wiki-authoring-spec` — for the readability rules and the list of every author-facing lookup.
**See also:** `wiki-template-labels` — for the grammar of the other docblock labels (Variants, Blocks, Columns, Excluded, Open body, Deviation).

## Section disposition

A template's docblock carries a `Disposition:` line naming which of its sections an authored page may drop — the property that makes a type's output structure deterministic. Every deployed template with body sections carries one; `redirect-stub` has none to dispose. A page author therefore always has a `Disposition:` line to read, whether or not they ever write one. The forms:

- **Default — `keep every header; "None." when empty.`** The section is structural and always relevant; an author with nothing to say writes `None.` rather than deleting the header, so the reader learns the page considered it. A dropped header leaves a structural trace but not a semantic one — a reader meeting a page without `## Lifecycle` cannot tell whether the subject has no lifecycle, the author never got to it, or the template had no such section when the page was written. Where the content has _relocated_ rather than emptied, the section carries a pointer instead of `None.`: name where it lives now, which tells the reader more than either a bare `None.` or an absence.
- **Variant — `pick one variant per the Variants line above`, or `omit the <X>-only sections per the Variants line above, which names them`.** The one way a header legitimately disappears. A distinct axis from Default: the page picks one shape up front, and that choice determines the section set. The `Variants:` line names each variant **and the sections it keeps** — except the variant the body scaffolds, whose set is the body itself: name that one as the body ("the scaffolded body below") and state every other variant as a delta from it, so adding a section to the body cannot leave the docblock asserting a stale set. `Disposition:` points at that line rather than restating the set, which would put one fact in two places on a single docblock. A template carrying shape variants it does not delegate a section set to still keeps its `Variants:` line — that duty attaches only where `Disposition:` points at it.

  The `Variants:` line's grammar is in `wiki-template-labels` §Template labels.

  **What is checked, and what is still judgment.** Which variant a page picked remains unverifiable when the page does not say — that is the recorded escape hatch, and review is its compensating control. What every variant _keeps_ is a different assertion needing no such knowledge, so `variant-sections` holds every page of the type to that intersection. A page may declare `variant: <Name>` to be held to that variant's whole set instead. The field is **optional by design**: requiring it would be a new frontmatter requirement, which raises the template's version, which would reclassify as legacy exactly the pages the check exists to surface.

- **`Pending: <event>.` — a value inside the Default form, not a fourth form.** A section its template's `Appends:` line declares reads `Pending: <event>.` until its event arrives; `wiki-page-state` §Page state axes holds the marker's grammar, its bounds and the spelling of each state a declared slot can be in.
- **Bullets — `mark an inapplicable bullet "None." rather than deleting it`.** Where a template's per-block content is bullets rather than headers (`ui-surface`, `ui-surface-impl`), Default governs every bullet exactly as it governs every header: a deleted bullet leaves no trace at all, and a dropped header leaves one that carries no meaning, so at neither granularity does absence communicate. A bullet may be split into qualified copies, `**<Label> (<qualifier>)**`, one per view; the copies together stand for the label. The block's own `##` headers take whichever form above applies.
- **A same-as pointer — `As [[design:surfaces/<module>/<feature-slug>#<surface-anchor>]]'s.`** On a bullet `table-columns.params.sameAs` lists, the pointer stands in for the table, saying this surface's table is another named surface's. Only the shared bullet takes one: a platform copy adds rows to the shared table, so a pointer on a copy is a bullet answered without its table, `table-columns`' error. `surface-same-as` errors on a pointer that is not a `design:` link to a named surface, that names its own surface, or that names a bullet that is `None.` or itself a pointer; a page stamped below the bullet's `cellsSince` version lists the finding as not yet required. Where the Input rules bullet is a pointer, the `input` and Required checks of `field-source` read the Input rules of the surface it names, and the rows its platform copies add.

**Required sections.** A template may name, on a `Required:` docblock label, the sections whose content a page may **not** answer with `None.` — the ones a page of this type exists to carry, and any its method requires. The Default form's `None.` is right for a section the author considered and had nothing to say about, and wrong for an `adr` with no decision or a `catalog` with no entries: there it reports that the page's own subject was considered and dismissed. It is as wrong for an `information-architecture` page with no structures considered, where it reports that the method's own step was skipped. `required-section-content` errors on a bare `None.` there, and on structure that says nothing — a table with a header and no rows. `Pending: <event>.` stays legal in a required section, because not-yet-due is a different state and the `Appends:` line owns it.

**A qualified heading.** A heading may carry a trailing qualifier naming which instance of the section it is — `## State boundary — copy-on-use snapshot` — and it stands for the declared section, exactly as a `**<Label> (<qualifier>)**` bullet stands for its declared label. Several qualified copies together stand for the one declared section.

**What a "section" means, and what counts as its content.** Every structural rule above is about `##` headings: a `###` heading is a block _inside_ a section, never a section, and no check reads one as a section title. A section's content is its prose and code lines. An HTML comment is **not** content, whether it sits in a section, a bullet's value or a table cell — a page that substitutes its frontmatter tokens and leaves every instruction comment intact carries empty sections, and `empty-section` reports them. A required frontmatter field is satisfied by a non-blank value; an empty list (`sources: []`) is blank, so a derived page shipping one has not satisfied the field.

**Section order.** A page carries its template's **declared** sections in the template's order. Undeclared sections may sit anywhere — a section the template does not name has no place in an order it is not part of, and interleaving one carries no functional consequence (a scenario-row parser reads per contiguous table run, not per section). A type that genuinely reads better in another order says so with a `Deviation:` label rather than letting each page choose; there is no per-page escape hatch, because an order that varies page to page is not an order.

**Every placeholder must be gone, in whichever form the template wrote it.** A template hands an author more than one kind of blank, and they are not interchangeable. `{{TOKEN}}` is a creation-time substitution — the title, the date, the confidence — and each template declares its own set on the `Substitute:` docblock line; `unsubstituted-token` reports one left behind. `<angle text>` is body content the author writes: a table cell, a bullet's value, a block heading's subject. It is declared nowhere, because the template's own text is the declaration — `unsubstituted-placeholder` reads the angle runs out of the deployed template and reports a page carrying one of them.
